We're delighted to share that TCW has been awarded Artsmark Platinum, the highest Arts Council England accreditation for creativity, arts and culture provision in schools.
Welcome to The Complete Works - a charity, a partnership of schools, a home for students who need something else from their education. At our schools we combine the highest of academic aspirations with an understanding that some students might want and need more than qualifications. That is why we treat every student as the unique individual they are. Our trained staff all believe in making their teaching tailored to the students they work with, embracing each personality, interest and dream and working in partnership towards these goals, whether they be personal skills, academic grades or steps to a new future.
Behind these passionate, skilled and empathetic teachers are an extensive team of experts creating bespoke learning journeys, personalised timetables and rigorous safety plans, while further teams offer wellbeing, qualified counselling and mentoring support.
The Complete Works is a creative company and this applies to everything we do, whether that be teaching the core academic subjects, delivering creative lessons or forming positive, professional, interesting relationships with our young people. Students also have the chance to express themselves creatively through a myriad of projects and performances, culminating in our big annual Showcase.
We work across London in students’ homes, local libraries and community centres, as well as in our specialised Learning Hubs. We teach students individually and in small groups to provide each young person with the right environment for them to be challenged and thrive.
By mixing and matching the elements of teachers, learning styles, subjects, locations and group size we intend to give everyone who comes to our schools an education that is built for them. I hope our website gives you a taste of some of the educational journeys our students have been on.
Adam Dalton - Executive Headteacher
“The Complete Works transforms pupils’ lives for the better and prepares them for the future exceptionally well.”
“The curriculum is aligned very skillfully to meet pupils’ specific needs and interests. There is an absolute focus on getting education right for each pupil.”
“The school’s unique education model meets pupils’ needs very effectively.”
What I need to say to all of you from the bottom of my heart is thank you. Thank you for your full support, thank you for your wonderful clear communication, thank you that you made a very tough traumatic time for us that bit easier , thank you for keeping my son amused happy and educated, thank you for keeping me amused and happy, but mostly Thank You all for being Fantastic.
My daughter has had a wonderful time at TCW. The impact it has had on her life is incredible - encouraging her to be the person she wants to be. Kai’s weekly counselling sessions have been greatly received, they always leave her mentally refreshed. It’s great to have this facility at hand every week so the young people feel they have someone to talk to and off load if they can’t do this at home. TCW saved her education because if she was to have stayed in main stream school she would not have the GCSEs she is leaving school with, so I am very grateful for every single person involved in the education and care of my daughter.
I don't know of any other educational provider which will go so far to engage a student in education, in whatever way and by whatever creative means suit's them. Both Liberty And Luke have been very responsive to Lawrence's needs, and ready to adapt and think creatively to help him. They have always been completely reliable, professional and inspiring.
I think that attending TCW has given our daughter an advantage that most of her peers in mainstream education don’t have. I have the greatest admiration for you all.
I just wanted to say briefly how amazing TCW is and has been for us. You basically saved our daughter's life over the past couple of years. And what you are doing for our son right now is invaluable. The understanding, flexibility and imagination exercised by the school and individual teachers makes all the difference in the world to young people, like our two for whom mainstream education was in no way a good fit.
My son is not at all keen on change and has for the first time found education so enjoyable and manageable. His teachers are exceptionally great with him.
TCW's one-to-one, individually tailored, creative and flexible approach to learning has enabled our son to learn and begin to prepare for his future in ways that truly work for him.
Thank you TCW for all your support and the wonderful work you do. My grandson has achieved more in TCW than any other school he has attended. Your fantastic team have helped him with his anxiety and social issues and have given him motivation and purpose and the will to learn.
It was fantastic seeing G perform on Tuesday - it must have taken huge amounts of confidence for her to do this which I think was a lot to do with how comfortable, accepted and supported she feels by everyone at TCW - particularly her teachers who spend many hours with her in the day time. Thank you for the amount you have done for her!
Just wanted to say a big thank you for all the support and kindness you have shown to W during his time at TCW. It is no exaggeration to say his life has been transformed thanks to the school's love and guidance.
I think it’s fair to say we were all blown away by S’s results yesterday! We’re so proud of her and we are so grateful to you and your amazing school.Without your flexibility, understanding and support we would not have been in this position now, where Sophia can carry on with her dreams in life without being held back.
I just wanted to take a moment to express my utmost appreciation and admiration for the complete works school. As a student here I have found it to be an amazing and enriching experience, largely due to the exceptional teachers who dedicate themselves to our education.
Thank you for all of the continued amazing individual support, and for the exceptional care from and expertise of all of your staff. We are incredibly grateful to have E in your school. We all realize how truly special it is!
After speaking to the mother today, it sounds like she is very happy about the progress that has been made and she was very grateful to the school for providing such great support, which has led to significant positive change in her and her family’s lives.
“Across year groups, the school provides an excellent range of enrichment and creative activities… These celebrate pupils’ achievements and expose them to the wider world.”
“The school is led and managed purposefully and with clear intent.”
“The arrangements for supporting staff and developing their expertise are very well coordinated… ensuring teachers have the knowledge, skills and expertise to implement the curriculum consistently well.”
“Staff carry out a careful and thorough analysis of pupils’ social, emotional and academic needs… enabling them to tailor teaching to pupils’ needs accurately.”
“Evidence of positivity is all around, from the very strong relationships and the creative approach to the curriculum to the calm and highly respectful culture.”
“Pupils are very well supported to develop their social, emotional and academic skills. Over time, pupils become increasingly engaged in learning and keen to do well.”
“Once pupils start at the school, their behaviour and attendance improve immeasurably.”

pageCache.pageTitle: TCW | Our ValuesThe Complete Works | Our Values
pageCache.text:
We're delighted to share that TCW has been awarded Artsmark Platinum, the highest Arts Council England accreditation for creativity, arts and culture provision in schools.
The Complete Works is synonymous with Creativity. From our beginning as a Theatre In Education Company, we have used creativity to unlock our students’ potential. It remains a key aspect of our school culture, underpinning the curriculum in every subject and is celebrated through an exciting range of extracurricular projects. Our teachers are trained to deliver dynamic and original lessons, tailored to the individual needs of each student.
What does true creativity mean? It is more than self-expression through the Arts. It means learning to think in original and insightful ways to solve problems. The best scientists, engineers and mathematicians are able to think outside the norm and make discoveries that shape the future. The creativity of entrepreneurs and business leaders will guide them toward emerging trends and capture the spirit of their market. In fact, it is hard to think of any job that when performed at the highest level, doesn’t benefit from a creative mindset and some originality of thought and approach.
The world our students are inheriting, is rapidly evolving. The advancements of technology and social change make it hard to imagine the landscape they will be navigating as adults. In these times of rapid change creativity is a vital skill. It allows us to contribute in unexpected and exciting ways and thrive no matter what the circumstances. It will be those young people who learned to think outside the box who will notice opportunities that others won’t. Those able to express themselves creatively, will help to keep us all grounded and fill our lives with insight and colour.
Over the years, our school has adapted to the challenges of unpredictable times, with creativity as a guiding principle. Whatever the future looks like, there will always be colour on our walls and the buzz of creativity in our classrooms.
Click here to learn more about Creativity at The Complete Works.
We prepare students for life, not just for exams. What we offer is academic, vocational, creative, social and emotional education. Lessons are taught on an individual basis and in small groups, supplemented with extracurricular creative projects and sector-leading pastoral support. This is a formula we have developed over many years, designed to help students grow as individuals and build the versatility and resilience required to be successful and happy throughout life.
We teach a wealth of academic and vocational subjects, from English, Maths and Science to Construction, Cooking, Photography, Animal Care and many more. Through the careful curating of individual and group lesson timetables, we help students to build confidence through manageable steps, while making meaningful connections with other young people. All students benefit from our signature creative style of learning and have access to a range of extra curricular projects - the TCW Album and Anthology, exhibitions at the Tate Modern and Whitechapel Galleries, to name a few. We offer Counselling and Personal Development programmes, as well as a targeted PSHE (Personal, Social and Health Education) curriculum, ensuring students receive the therapeutic and pastoral support they need to work through their personal challenges, freeing up mental space for learning and inner growth.
We design bespoke education packages to fit the unique needs, interests, personality and ambitions of every student, helping them to feel understood and validated as individuals. Over the years, we have become renowned for the flexibility of our approach, curating a different experience for every student so they can each learn in their own way. Our lessons are taught on an individual basis or in small groups, so we can cater to every learning style. We have an expert curriculum team to oversee the learning pathways of all students and ensure that they are getting the best possible experience to match their individual requirements.
Our celebration of individuality comes from a deep belief in the value of walking your own path in life. We recognise the great diversity of young people in our cohort, the different challenges they have faced and the uniqueness of each perspective they bring. This allows students to learn from each other and be enriched by their differences. Throughout a student’s educational journey we encourage them to develop new interests and discover their own path. We are here to support and guide them along every step of the way.
Learning is a lifelong process. We work to instil this belief in all our students, helping them to approach life with curiosity and openness, exploring divergent points of view, developing objectivity and empathy to last them far beyond their school years. This is Open-Mindedness - a value we cultivate in ourselves as teachers, as much as in our students. All TCW Staff continue to learn and develop throughout their careers, taking part in regular professional development to further hone their skills and keep them up to date with emerging knowledge. No matter our level of experience, we should always be ready for new learning. There is so much out there to discover, if we keep our minds open!
Every student is different and part of the joy of working at TCW is getting to know such a diverse range of young people and finding a way to adapt to their unique criteria of needs. We believe that teachers should learn from their students - understanding them as individuals and celebrating their interests. It takes open-mindedness to find a truly effective way to connect with and teach a new student, particularly one whose needs and personal challenges set them outside the typical mainstream school mould. Over the years, we have welcomed countless young people into our school community, giving them the sense of belonging and validation they have struggled so much to find. Everyone is welcome at The Complete Works and, to quote Paddington, because “everyone is different, that means anyone can fit in.”
Holistic Education
Individuality
Open Mindedness

We're delighted to share that TCW has been awarded Artsmark Platinum, the highest Arts Council England accreditation for creativity, arts and culture provision in schools.
Much A-Brew About Nothing is a community coffee shop, run by The Complete Works Charity. Nestled just off Brick Lane, it’s a warm and welcoming space - a haven from the bustle of city life, where you can pause, connect with neighbours, and enjoy exceptional coffee and scrumptious bites.
At Much A-Brew, we conduct our Hospitality and Work Experience programmes, as well as student-led creative events. Every brew directly supports our work with young people, helping them gain the skills, confidence, and opportunities they need to shape their futures.
Why a Cafe?
We are always looking for new ways to broaden the educational experience of our students. Over the years, we have enriched our curriculum, strengthened our pastoral support, developed a sector-leading teacher training programme, and used creativity to bring every subject to life.
The next step in our journey is to offer real-world work experience programme that bridges the gap between the highly bespoke, nurturing education students receive here and the more unpredictable world of work. That’s where Much A-Brew comes in.
Young people from The Complete Works are part of the team running the cafe. With guidance from experienced mentors, they learn what it takes to operate a real business - from customer service and food safety to event planning and teamwork. This is real world, practical learning that will serve them far beyond the classroom. By working alongside our team in the café, students gain confidence, employability skills, and a sense of achievement that prepares them for their future.
The name Much A-Brew About Nothing is a nod to our Shakespearean roots and a playful reminder that sometimes, we all need to pause, share a brew, and have a natter about nothing much at all.
Our Cafe Work Experience Programme
Led by industry professionals and supported by specialist SEN teachers, our work experience programme offers practical learning in a safe, creative, and inclusive environment.
The programme includes:
One day per week in the café, gaining hands-on experience in catering, customer service, and events, with the opportunity to achieve an industry-standard Food Hygiene qualification.
One day per week in the classroom, studying Maths and English up to GCSE level, alongside Life Skills sessions taught in small groups at a TCW Learning Hub.
Weekly careers coaching, with one hour of personalised support focused on CV writing, interview preparation, and planning future employment pathways.
Throughout the programme, students work towards a BTEC Level 1 in Hospitality & Tourism.

We're delighted to share that TCW has been awarded Artsmark Platinum, the highest Arts Council England accreditation for creativity, arts and culture provision in schools.
Safer Recruitment Compliance - A Statement of Assurance
The Complete Works Independent School (TCW) is a registered Independent School and the safety and welfare of our students is of paramount importance. We are committed to meeting all statutory safeguarding and safer recruitment requirements required by KCSIE 2025.
TCW confirms that every member of staff is fully vetted in line with statutory safer recruitment guidance. No member of staff begins work with TCW until all required checks have been fully completed and verified.
All staff at The Complete Works are subject to:
• Enhanced DBS check
• Two suitable written references from previous employers
• Online search checks
• Selection and interview with Safer Recruitment trained staff
• Safeguarding training to the appropriate level
• Full induction programme, including safeguarding focus
• Weekly ongoing training, including safeguarding, mental health and welfare
• Regular monitoring and checks on safeguarding standards and reporting
• Individual 1:1 support offer from a qualified BACP School Counsellor
• Regular line management
Teachers additionally receive:
• Line management from an experienced Teaching & Learning Officer who holds QTS.
• Two lesson observations conducted during the probationary period
• Ongoing support from experienced Subject Consultants who hold QTS.
We strictly follow all safer recruitment, safeguarding and child protection policies, which are current and apply to learners from Key Stage 1 to post-18. Staff wear clearly identifiable ID badges and are required to sign a declaration confirming they have read and understood KCSIE (Part 1) and the TCW Safeguarding Policy upon arrival.
This represents formal written confirmation that TCW follows full Safer Recruitment practice, in line with DfE requirements and statutory guidance for alternative education providers.

pageCache.text:
We're delighted to share that TCW has been awarded Artsmark Platinum, the highest Arts Council England accreditation for creativity, arts and culture provision in schools.
All of Us
Together we make up over 100 staff, including Teachers, Student Welfare Officers and specialists in Safeguarding, Wellbeing, Curriculum, SEN, Logistics and Teacher Training. To name a few! We believe our students deserve a completely bespoke educational experience, designed to be as unique as they are. This requires a coordinated approach between a large team of experts. Here we are - the 2025, Ofsted Outstanding team!
Executive Team
As Chief Executive Officer, Chrissie oversees the strategic direction of the charity, ensuring all activities adhere to the charity's objectives and follow the founding principles created by Phil Richards. Chrissie works closely with the Founder and Executive Headteacher on the development of the TCW school and works alongside the Financial Controller to oversee the charity finances. Chrissie has been with TCW since 2003 as Education and Creative coordinator and then as Deputy Chief Executive for 12 years, before being appointed Chief Executive in 2016. Chrissie has a background in acting and singing and believes creativity in all its forms, alongside bespoke education and individualised support, can enhance a young person's experience of school life and improve their life chances.
As Executive Headteacher, Adam oversees the development and strategic direction of The Complete Works as a whole, including education across our East and South London Schools. Alongside CEO, Chrissie, he leads the Central Team, ensuring the standard of provision across all sites is in line with the unique values and identity of TCW. Adam has worked at TCW since 2003, originally as an offsite teacher, then running some of TCW's first onsite centres before becoming Head of School and finally Headteacher in 2016. Adam has a MBA in Educational Leadership from the UCL Institute for Education and previously worked as an actor in the West End.
Karina has been with TCW for over ten years. She began her career as a one to one teacher and later helped to set up our first onsite provisions, in which she worked as a group teacher and then Head of Centre. From here, Karina moved to the office team as Creative Coordinator, using her skills, contacts and expertise in the creative world gained from her MA in Screen Acting. She now oversees curriculum, creativity and teaching and learning as our Director of Education.
As Director of Operations, Amy oversees the HR department, Safeguarding, Admissions and Communications. Prior to this, Amy led the Curriculum and Exams teams. Amy has worked at TCW since 2013, starting as an Education Coordinator before moving onto Curriculum Manager. Amy has a BA in Performing Arts and previously worked in Secondary and Primary schools and youth theatres teaching acting and dance to children and young people.
Andy took on the role of Headteacher of the South London School in August 2024, prior to which he was Assistant Head, overseeing Personal Development, Interventions, Staff Training and CPD. Andy joined TCW in 2005 and has had a number of different roles, including Head of Interventions, Behaviour and Attendance. Andy has an MA in Performance in Recorded Media and is currently training in performance coaching. His main passion away from school is his family and Tottenham Hotspur Football Club.
Dean took on the role of Headteacher in August 2024, prior to which he oversaw Operations, SEN, and Attendance and Behaviour in his role as Assistant Head. Dean has worked at TCW since 2015, in which time he has been instrumental to the development of our educational and wellbeing offer. He is currently studying an MBA in Senior Leadership and has previously worked in primary schools, community day centres for adults with learning difficulties and as a musician.
Chrissie Roberts CEO
Karina Cornwell Director of Education
Amy Jones Director of Operations
Andy Davies Headteacher - South London School
Dean Phillips-Smith Headteacher - East London School
Our Founder
Phil Richards trained as a theatre practitioner at the Rose Bruford College of Theatre and Performance. He taught for 20 years in mainstream schools, which included running the Drama Department at the Brit School of Performing Arts. He has also worked extensively with students who have disabilities, special educational needs and emotional and behavioural difficulties. He teaches on the PGCE Drama course at Goldsmiths University of London and runs inset courses on using creative methods of interaction across the curriculum. He founded The Complete Works in partnership with the late Neil Powney, in 1999. Click here to read Phil's story.
Phil Richards Founder
Central Team
The Central Team oversees the running of The Complete Works as a whole, ensuring both schools stay true to the values, ethos and methods that have proven so effective over the years. The primary goals of the Central Team are to coordinate and quality assure the student experience; to give teachers all the support they need to deliver inspiring lessons, and to keep the inner workings of both schools running smoothly. This involves a number of departments all working together, including: Teaching & Learning, Curriculum, Safeguarding & Wellbeing, Attendance & Behaviour, Creativity, HR, Finance, and Communications.
As Financial Controller, Jasmin oversees all of the finances and budgets for the school, and governance for the charity. She has been with TCW since 2023, and works closely with the Senior Leadership Team and Trustees. Jasmin holds a BSC Honours in Finance and Economics from QMC and is in the final stages of completing her training to become a Chartered Accountant. Jasmin has over 12 years of experience in the not-for-profit sector.
Ross is the Head of Safeguarding & Wellbeing, and also leads on Health & Safety. Over the last 20 years, Ross has gained a broad range of experience in safeguarding. He has worked as a community volunteer, a frontline worker with vulnerable children and families, as well as setting up and running multiple intervention and support programmes with a wide variety of teams, including local authorities, schools and other organisations, to practically and strategically improve safeguarding.
As the Head of Admissions, Tina is responsible for overseeing all referrals and consultations made to TCW. This involves close collaboration with our Senior Leadership Team (SLT) to assess student documents, ensuring that we can effectively cater to their specific requirements. Tina also maintains regular communication with local authorities and other professionals involved in supporting the young people we serve.Tina's journey at TCW began in 2007 when she joined as the Financial Controller. In 2010 Tina was appointed as the Office Manager and in 2018 began in her current position as the Head of Admissions.
Kayleigh heads up our Teaching and Learning Team, overseeing the support and development of TCW teachers through training, observations and mentoring. With eight years experience as an onsite TCW teacher, she offers supportive observations for the wider teaching team and helps in the planning and delivery of training sessions. Kayleigh has a background in drama and education and has used this experience to bring creativity to all her roles at TCW.
Matt is our Head of Curriculum. He joined TCW in 2018, originally as Exams and Data Officer. Prior to this, Matt spent 2 years as a Learning Support Officer working with SEN students in a mainstream school after earning a Master's Degree in Chemistry. Matt leads the development of the school's curriculum and oversees post-16 progression routes. When it comes to sports, puzzles and musicals, he is a fountain of knowledge.
As HR Coordinator, Dylan is a key point of contact for staff at TCW, helping to maintain a happy and motivated workforce. He oversees the logistics of recruitment and employee relations and works alongside the HR Officer and the Communications Officer to ensure an effective HR service is provided within the charity and school.
Tanzil serves as the IT Manager at The Complete Works, where he oversees the company's technology infrastructure and ensures smooth operations across all systems. With a background in IT management, he is dedicated to optimising workflows and enhancing digital security. Outside of work, Tanzil is also a musician, performing during weekends.
As our Interventions Officer, Tyrone works with students needing support with their attendance, engagement or motivation. In his ten years at TCW, Ty was a one to one teacher for five years, before specialising in helping our most disengaged students to rediscover their interest in learning. Ty works directly with students, as well as their families, professionals and teachers to improve attendance and engagement in lessons.
Amrit is the Head of HR at TCW and holds responsibility for ensuring compliance with legislation and maintaining adherence to policies and procedures within the school. Her responsibilities span various areas, including recruitment, career development, performance management, coaching, and providing guidance and support to the staff. Amrit actively contributes to the establishment of a diverse and inclusive environment by implementing effective HR strategies aligned with TCW's core values. She is also a Mental Health First Aider.
Eleanor works closely with the Executive Headteacher and the Senior Leadership Team to ensure the smooth running of the schools. Before abandoning Yorkshire and becoming an honorary southerner, she held admin roles at Network Rail. Outside of The Complete Works, she performs in a function band and teaches singing privately.
Andrew is a member of the finance team and looks after incoming and outgoing payments. He is also responsible for payroll and school expenses. Prior to TCW, Andrew worked in finance for the NHS.
In his role as Head of Creative Learning, Christian is responsible for making sure every student has opportunities to develop their creativity, both through the curriculum and extra-curricular enrichment projects. Creativity is a core value of TCW and Christian's role is key in bringing this value to life. As Poet in Residence, Christian works with each student, with the aim of producing poetry, music, film or podcasts. Each year, he collates our student work into an album and a published anthology. To date, we have released seven albums and ten anthologies. We're delighted to share that TCW has been awarded Artsmark Platinum, the highest Arts Council England accreditation for creativity, arts and culture provision in schools.
Much A-Brew About Nothing is a community coffee shop, run by The Complete Works Charity. Nestled just off Brick Lane, it’s a warm and welcoming space - a haven from the bustle of city life, where you can pause, connect with neighbours, and enjoy exceptional coffee and scrumptious bites.
At Much A-Brew, we conduct our Hospitality and Work Experience programmes, as well as student-led creative events. Every brew directly supports our work with young people, helping them gain the skills, confidence, and opportunities they need to shape their futures.
Why a Cafe?
We are always looking for new ways to broaden the educational experience of our students. Over the years, we have enriched our curriculum, strengthened our pastoral support, developed a sector-leading teacher training programme, and used creativity to bring every subject to life.
The next step in our journey is to offer real-world work experience programme that bridges the gap between the highly bespoke, nurturing education students receive here and the more unpredictable world of work. That’s where Much A-Brew comes in.
Young people from The Complete Works are part of the team running the cafe. With guidance from experienced mentors, they learn what it takes to operate a real business - from customer service and food safety to event planning and teamwork. This is real world, practical learning that will serve them far beyond the classroom. By working alongside our team in the café, students gain confidence, employability skills, and a sense of achievement that prepares them for their future.
The name Much A-Brew About Nothing is a nod to our Shakespearean roots and a playful reminder that sometimes, we all need to pause, share a brew, and have a natter about nothing much at all.
Our Cafe Work Experience Programme
Led by industry professionals and supported by specialist SEN teachers, our work experience programme offers practical learning in a safe, creative, and inclusive environment.
The programme includes:
One day per week in the café, gaining hands-on experience in catering, customer service, and events, with the opportunity to achieve an industry-standard Food Hygiene qualification.
One day per week in the classroom, studying Maths and English up to GCSE level, alongside Life Skills sessions taught in small groups at a TCW Learning Hub.
Weekly careers coaching, with one hour of personalised support focused on CV writing, interview preparation, and planning future employment pathways.
Throughout the programme, students work towards a BTEC Level 1 in Hospitality & Tourism.

We're delighted to share that TCW has been awarded Artsmark Platinum, the highest Arts Council England accreditation for creativity, arts and culture provision in schools.
Safer Recruitment Compliance - A Statement of Assurance
The Complete Works Independent School (TCW) is a registered Independent School and the safety and welfare of our students is of paramount importance. We are committed to meeting all statutory safeguarding and safer recruitment requirements required by KCSIE 2025.
TCW confirms that every member of staff is fully vetted in line with statutory safer recruitment guidance. No member of staff begins work with TCW until all required checks have been fully completed and verified.
All staff at The Complete Works are subject to:
• Enhanced DBS check
• Two suitable written references from previous employers
• Online search checks
• Selection and interview with Safer Recruitment trained staff
• Safeguarding training to the appropriate level
• Full induction programme, including safeguarding focus
• Weekly ongoing training, including safeguarding, mental health and welfare
• Regular monitoring and checks on safeguarding standards and reporting
• Individual 1:1 support offer from a qualified BACP School Counsellor
• Regular line management
Teachers additionally receive:
• Line management from an experienced Teaching & Learning Officer who holds QTS.
• Two lesson observations conducted during the probationary period
• Ongoing support from experienced Subject Consultants who hold QTS.
We strictly follow all safer recruitment, safeguarding and child protection policies, which are current and apply to learners from Key Stage 1 to post-18. Staff wear clearly identifiable ID badges and are required to sign a declaration confirming they have read and understood KCSIE (Part 1) and the TCW Safeguarding Policy upon arrival.
This represents formal written confirmation that TCW follows full Safer Recruitment practice, in line with DfE requirements and statutory guidance for alternative education providers.

All of Us
Together we make up over 100 staff, including Teachers, Student Welfare Officers and specialists in Safeguarding, Wellbeing, Curriculum, SEN, Logistics and Teacher Training. To name a few! We believe our students deserve a completely bespoke educational experience, designed to be as unique as they are. This requires a coordinated approach between a large team of experts. Here we are - the 2025, Ofsted Outstanding team!
Executive Team

Chrissie works closely with the Founder and Executive Headteacher on the development of the TCW school and works alongside the Financial Controller to oversee the charity finances. Chrissie has been with TCW since 2003 as Education and Creative coordinator and then as Deputy Chief Executive for 12 years, before being appointed Chief Executive in 2016. Chrissie has a background in acting and singing and believes creativity in all its forms, alongside bespoke education and individualised support, can enhance a young person's experience of school life and improve their life chances.
As Executive Headteacher, Adam oversees the development and strategic direction of The Complete Works as a whole, including education across our East and South London Schools. Alongside CEO, Chrissie, he leads the Central Team, ensuring the standard of provision across all sites is in line with the unique values and identity of TCW. Adam has worked at TCW since 2003, originally as an offsite teacher, then running some of TCW's first onsite centres before becoming Head of School and finally Headteacher in 2016. Adam has a MBA in Educational Leadership from the UCL Institute for Education and previously worked as an actor in the West End.
Karina has been with TCW for over ten years. She began her career as a one to one teacher and later helped to set up our first onsite provisions, in which she worked as a group teacher and then Head of Centre. From here, Karina moved to the office team as Creative Coordinator, using her skills, contacts and expertise in the creative world gained from her MA in Screen Acting. She now oversees curriculum, creativity and teaching and learning as our Director of Education.
As Director of Operations, Amy oversees the HR department, Safeguarding, Admissions and Communications. Prior to this, Amy led the Curriculum and Exams teams. Amy has worked at TCW since 2013, starting as an Education Coordinator before moving onto Curriculum Manager. Amy has a BA in Performing Arts and previously worked in Secondary and Primary schools and youth theatres teaching acting and dance to children and young people.
Andy took on the role of Headteacher of the South London School in August 2024, prior to which he was Assistant Head, overseeing Personal Development, Interventions, Staff Training and CPD. Andy joined TCW in 2005 and has had a number of different roles, including Head of Interventions, Behaviour and Attendance. Andy has an MA in Performance in Recorded Media and is currently training in performance coaching. His main passion away from school is his family and Tottenham Hotspur Football Club.
Dean took on the role of Headteacher in August 2024, prior to which he oversaw Operations, SEN, and Attendance and Behaviour in his role as Assistant Head. Dean has worked at TCW since 2015, in which time he has been instrumental to the development of our educational and wellbeing offer. He is currently studying an MBA in Senior Leadership and has previously worked in primary schools, community day centres for adults with learning difficulties and as a musician.

Our Founder
Phil Richards trained as a theatre practitioner at the Rose Bruford College of Theatre and Performance. He taught for 20 years in mainstream schools, which included running the Drama Department at the Brit School of Performing Arts. He has also worked extensively with students who have disabilities, special educational needs and emotional and behavioural difficulties. He teaches on the PGCE Drama course at Goldsmiths University of London and runs inset courses on using creative methods of interaction across the curriculum. He founded The Complete Works in partnership with the late Neil Powney, in 1999. Click here to read Phil's story.
Phil Richards Founder

The primary goals of the Central Team are to coordinate and quality assure the student experience; to give teachers all the support they need to deliver inspiring lessons, and to keep the inner workings of both schools running smoothly. This involves a number of departments all working together, including: Teaching & Learning, Curriculum, Safeguarding & Wellbeing, Attendance & Behaviour, Creativity, HR, Finance, and Communications.
As Financial Controller, Jasmin oversees all of the finances and budgets for the school, and governance for the charity. She has been with TCW since 2023, and works closely with the Senior Leadership Team and Trustees. Jasmin holds a BSC Honours in Finance and Economics from QMC and is in the final stages of completing her training to become a Chartered Accountant. Jasmin has over 12 years of experience in the not-for-profit sector.
Ross is the Head of Safeguarding & Wellbeing, and also leads on Health & Safety. Over the last 20 years, Ross has gained a broad range of experience in safeguarding. He has worked as a community volunteer, a frontline worker with vulnerable children and families, as well as setting up and running multiple intervention and support programmes with a wide variety of teams, including local authorities, schools and other organisations, to practically and strategically improve safeguarding.
As the Head of Admissions, Tina is responsible for overseeing all referrals and consultations made to TCW. This involves close collaboration with our Senior Leadership Team (SLT) to assess student documents, ensuring that we can effectively cater to their specific requirements. Tina also maintains regular communication with local authorities and other professionals involved in supporting the young people we serve.Tina's journey at TCW began in 2007 when she joined as the Financial Controller. In 2010 Tina was appointed as the Office Manager and in 2018 began in her current position as the Head of Admissions.
Kayleigh heads up our Teaching and Learning Team, overseeing the support and development of TCW teachers through training, observations and mentoring. With eight years experience as an onsite TCW teacher, she offers supportive observations for the wider teaching team and helps in the planning and delivery of training sessions. Kayleigh has a background in drama and education and has used this experience to bring creativity to all her roles at TCW.
Matt is our Head of Curriculum. He joined TCW in 2018, originally as Exams and Data Officer. Prior to this, Matt spent 2 years as a Learning Support Officer working with SEN students in a mainstream school after earning a Master's Degree in Chemistry. Matt leads the development of the school's curriculum and oversees post-16 progression routes. When it comes to sports, puzzles and musicals, he is a fountain of knowledge.
